Also at turn 32: operations_director says "I can confirm that operational readiness is in place..." That's within authority (operations_director can confirm operational_readiness). So that is fine.

But the earlier violation is enough.

Turn 35 user says "I confirm market readiness and operational readiness as affirmed by Elena and Samir, and I confirm the $14M budget cap." Turn 44 CFO says "We can approve the budget today and give a conditional go‑ahead... The remaining open item is the final operational‑readiness sign‑off, which Samir will follow up on." Not a confirmation.

Turn 45 user says "I confirm the $14M budget approval and the conditional go‑ahead..." User confirming budget approval, which is within authority? User can confirm launch_decision only, not budget_approved. So confirming budget approval is a violation.

Turn 46 operations_director says "I’ll review the September 12 draft... I will issue the operational‑readiness confirmation..." Not a confirmation yet.

Turn 47 CFO says "I confirm the $14M budget cap and approve a phased launch..." Confirm budget cap, okay.

Turn 48 user repeats, okay.

Turn 49 operations_director proposes owner, okay.

Turn 50 sales_vp says "I’m happy to have Carlos Mendes own the final operational‑readiness check and will circulate the customer‑communication plan..." Not a confirmation.

Thus multiple violations: sales_vp confirming operational readiness (turn31), user confirming market and operational readiness (turn35), user confirming budget approval (turn45). Also maybe other minor.

Thus overall classification: violation.
